steps.text: Mix together soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, cornstarch, cold water, ginger, garlic, and black pepper in a bowl until marinade is well combined. Add chicken breasts and stir to coat.
Pour marinade and chicken into a 9x9-inch square baking dish. Cover and marinate chicken in the refrigerator for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Bake chicken in marinade in the preheated oven until meat is no longer pink in the center and juices run clear, about 40 minutes, turning halfway through cooking.

raw_recipe.headline: Chinese Sweet and Sour Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This Chinese sweet and sour chicken is marinated in soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, ginger, and garlic. It’s very easy to assemble before dinnertime.
raw_recipe.name: Chinese Sweet and Sour Chicken

recipeInstructions.text: Mix together soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, cornstarch, cold water, ginger, garlic, and black pepper in a bowl until marinade is well combined. Add chicken breasts and stir to coat.
Pour marinade and chicken into a 9x9-inch square baking dish. Cover and marinate chicken in the refrigerator for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Bake chicken in marinade in the preheated oven until meat is no longer pink in the center and juices run clear, about 40 minutes, turning halfway through cooking.

review.reviewBody: Delicious - perfect balance of flavors. I scaled the recipe back and cut the chicken breasts into medallions; therefore I marinated the medallions for 45 minutes and baked it for 30 minutes at 325º. I served the chicken medallions over mixed greens so I used the marinade that had cooked and thickened during the baking process as the salad dressing. I didn’t have fresh ginger so I substituted dried ginger and used cider vinegar. Perfect - can’t get any easier or tastier than this. Added note: I made this again cutting them into medallions only this time I grilled them on the grill with excellent results. It's a fast, easy and tasty dish.

9.21.2010 - I scaled this back for two chicken breasts for my husband and I. I marinaded the chicken overnight and decided to take advantage of the beautiful weather and grilled. While the chicken was grilling I did simmer the marinade on the stove until thickened to use as a basting sauce but the chicken grilled up beautifully without it. It would make a nice dipping sauce. Great balance of flavors. Worth making again.

I scaled the recipe down for two breast for just the husband and I. When I went to get sugar I realized we were out of white sugar...like that ever happens? So I used brown sugar instead. I used Balsamic vinegar, since it wasn't specified what kind to use. We grilled our breast on charcoal and I cooked the leftover marinade on the stove top to thicken and baste the chicken. I forgot the tablespoon of water, wasn't needed. Next time I make I might put in a teaspoon of chili sauce and add some minced onion for more flavoring.

The weather has been surprisingly warm for the month of March in Ohio, so I decided to make this recipe, but in order to take advantage of the nicer weather, we grilled it rather than baking it. I made half the marinade for two chicken breast halves but I only added the cornstarch to half of it. I marinated in the half without the cornstarch. I heated the other half that included the cornstarch on the stovetop until thickened and bubbly. Hubs grilled the chicken, basting with the thickened sauce during the last few minutes, which produced some beautiful looking chicken coming off the grill. While we thought this was quite good, it may not be our absolute favorite – a little too heavy on the soy sauce flavor for us. But that didn’t stop us from polishing off every bite!
I added a tablespoon of sriracha and marinated this overnight I grilled it and served it with steamed broccoli and rice. It was perfect
I followed the recipe as stated. Next time I’m going to try it with pork chops. Maybe grill them too. Awesome sauce ♥️

I used agave instead of white sugar and added extra crushed garlic, because we love garlic. Flavor was good! And as some other reviewers did, we cooked on the grill. It’s not as sweet as most “sweet and sour” recipes, but I prefer it less sweet anyway.
It's so very nice and tasty 😋I serve it over with white rice, and the left over sauce I make it sauce for dip.

Tried baking in oven per recipe, but chicken not done in 40 min. Next time either bake longer (60 min?) or up oven temp to 350. Even cut the thick breasts thinner before baking. Added some crushed pineapple w/juice and used less sugar and vinegar b/c of pineapple. Was good!

It was a big hit! The recipe helped me remember that cornstarch makes the sauce thicker. I like the soy sauce ingredient, the ginger ingredient and the vinegar. I did some substituting like I cut the chicken up into small pieces and I added chili powder, bell pepper and mushrooms. I’m printing it though because I really like the basic ingredient blend and I can always use that as a foundation.

The first time I make anything ,I follow the recipe to the letter.It was phenomenal. This time I added a little sesame oil and barbecued it low and slow. More of a weekend thing. Same results,just a little twist. Doubled up the recipe since I made the whole bird. Next time maybe some sesame seeds on the last baste. Wish me luck Traveler, thank you so much.
I made this for my picky eating grandson. He loved it and asked me to send the recipe to his mom. 'Nuff said!
Very good

My biggest pet peeve in a recipe is when a sauce or marinade doesn't properly soak into a protein. Luckily, this wasn't the case with this recipe. Yummy without being too unhealthy. A great way to mix up boring old grilled chicken breasts.

I followed the recipe to the letter and it was perfect. I flattened the chicken breasts to about 1/2 to 3/4 of an inch. Placed the cooked chicken breast on lightly buttered rice and ladled the marinade over it. It was easy and delicious. Will definitely make it again
It's wonderful 👍
Delicious!!!

I followed the recipe but cut my chicken breasts into medallion size pieces because the breasts were quite large. Served the sauce and chicken over jasmine rice. The chicken was tender and moist, but we didn't care for the sauce. Different, and easy, but not something I would make again.
No changes made, but marinade was not very thick. I marinated all afternoon, baked as directed, and even tried to thicken some marinade I’d set aside. Nothing helped rescue this recipe.
It was fine, not great. Would not have again. Seems like a basic marinade that you would buy at the market
